Marathon Petroleum stock climbed 2.3% today as oil prices surged to a six-week high following renewed military tensions between Iran and the U.S. in the Middle East over the weekend. Crude hit nearly $99 per barrel—a significant jump from recent levels—and with U.S. refineries running at 98% capacity, higher oil prices typically improve refining margins (the profit spread between what refiners pay for crude and what they collect selling finished fuels like gasoline and diesel). The stock's 9.7% gain over two weeks tracks closely with this escalating geopolitical risk premium pushing energy prices higher.

The broader tailwind here is tight refining conditions: storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain relatively lean at current demand levels, which means refiners have pricing power when crude spikes. Geopolitical disruptions that threaten Middle Eastern oil supply—a route critical to global energy flows—tend to lift the entire refining sector's profitability.
